1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the checkout, until the checkout's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first checkout: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the tools, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	uv run runs.py | tail -3                                           # the last run records, as rows of the table
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and the wire, `wire.jsonl` fresh from a build and `wire.jsonl.gz` once committed. `uv run runs.py` is every record's numbers as one table. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `head` is the red commit it started from.
27	- `cases/` is the evaluation set: one directory per case, a goal and a red test against this repository's own code, each probing a known way for the builder to fail. `uv run evals.py` runs every case three times in throwaway worktrees and prints one table per case; its records are ordinary records whose goal begins `case: <name>`, so `runs.py` shows them beside the builds.
28	
29	## How a version is made
30	
31	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the checkout and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, compresses its wire to `wire.jsonl.gz`, commits both as the factory's work, and hands the diff to an independent reviewer, a fresh session in this harness that reads the Goal, the diff and the tests and probes the change in throwaway directories; a defect the review finds, once the attended agent has verified it, becomes a test and a follow-up build on the same seed. When every seed of the version is done, the attended agent revises this file, writes the version note's changelog, fast-forwards `main` and runs `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate refuses until everything derived agrees, then cuts the annotated tag and renders `CHANGELOG.md`. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the tools refuse the model the same.
32	
33	## Commands
34	
35	- `uv run gate.py check`, `uv run gate.py render`, `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate. Problems go to stdout, one per line, starting with the path; exit 1 when there is any, 2 for a usage error, silence and 0 otherwise. `render` writes `CHANGELOG.md`. `release` also needs a clean tree, `AGENTS.md` changed since the previous tag, a green suite and at least one changelog bullet in the version note.
36	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
37	- `uv run runs.py`: the records as a tab-separated table, one row per record, a header first; nothing is written. Any argument is a usage error.
38	- `uv run evals.py [--runs N] [case ...]`: the evaluation set, every case N times (three by default) in throwaway worktrees of this repository at `HEAD`, the case's files and test committed there first; one tab-separated table of counts (green, honest, refused) and medians per case. Needs the key and docker like a build; the records land in `runs/` like a build's. Exit 1 when any run was capped or errored, 2 for a usage error.
39	- `uv run builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the checkout's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Refuses a directory that is not a git checkout, and a checkout with uncommitted or untracked changes, exit 2. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the checkout. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error. The cost and the time are in the record.
40	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a checkout for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
41	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
42	
43	## Not derivable from the repository
44	
45	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. `backlog.base` changes whenever the owner adjusts a view, a filter or an order there, and a note's frontmatter is re-serialised when a property is edited there, in Obsidian's own shape; a frontmatter value that is not valid YAML, such as a bare `{{date}}`, does not survive that. A dirty `docs/` is the owner's content: read the diff and commit it as theirs.
46	- A version exists only as a tag. Commit 48cbbe4 is titled `v0.4`; it is one change released in v0.4, not the version.
47	- The notes of v0.1 to v0.4, their changelog and the records before v0.5 say world for the checkout and plane for the tools; those were the observer's words.
48	- Branches `bootstrap` and `v0.1` to `v0.3` are leftovers of past worktrees and share their names with the tags, so git warns and prefers the tag. Write `tags/v0.3` where it matters.
49	- The model is DeepSeek `deepseek-flash`. pydantic-ai does not know the name, so `builder.py` carries a profile override; genai-prices has no row for it, so the price table in `builder.py` is the cost source. Thinking is on by default and ignores temperature. The key is never printed or committed.
50	- The history before this repository, v1 and the design that was abandoned for it, is in the owner's Obsidian vault at `/srv/obsidian/vaults/obsidian/03 archive/factory-v1/`. Reference, never a plan.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The evaluation harness: run the builder over a set of cases and tabulate the runs.
3	
4	    uv run evals.py [--runs N] [case ...]
5	
6	A case is a directory `cases/<name>/` under the repository holding `goal.md`, exactly one
7	`test_<name>.py`, and optionally `files/`. Each case runs N times (three unless `--runs N`), each
8	run in a throwaway git worktree of the repository at HEAD: the case's `files/` and test are
9	committed there as `case: <name>` by `factory <factory@localhost>`, the builder runs on that
10	worktree, and the worktree is removed and pruned whether the run succeeded or not. The records
11	land in the repository's `runs/`, where the builder leaves them, so every run is one more record
12	and the goal's first line names the case. Nothing here changes the repository the worktrees are
13	cut from.
14	
15	When every run is done one tab-separated table is printed: a header, then one row per case in the
16	order given, with the counts of green, honest and refused runs and the medians of the builder's
17	numbers. Exit 0 when every run ended with the `answer` answer, 1 when any run was capped or
18	errored, 2 on stderr for a usage error (a case that does not exist or is not whole, or a run
19	count that is not a positive integer).
20	"""
21	
22	from __future__ import annotations
23	
24	import contextlib
25	import io
26	import json
27	import shutil
28	import statistics
29	import sys
30	import tempfile
31	from pathlib import Path
32	from typing import Any
33	
34	import builder
35	
36	DEFAULT_RUNS = 3
37	COLUMNS = (
38	    "case", "runs", "green", "honest", "refused", "requests", "tool_calls", "edits", "checks",
39	    "input_per_request", "cost_usd", "seconds", "cost_total", "diff_lines", "files_changed",
40	    "deletions", "stray_files",
41	)  # fmt: skip
42	# A run's medians are taken over its own numbers: every column a record may lack, and the
43	# derived input-per-request and diff-lines, which are computed here the way runs.py computes them.
44	MEDIAN_COLUMNS = (
45	    "requests", "tool_calls", "edits", "checks", "input_per_request", "cost_usd", "seconds",
46	)  # fmt: skip
47	REFUSED = ("error: protected", "error: not part of", "error: outside")
48	
49	
50	def usage_error(reason: str = "") -> int:
51	    print("usage: evals.py [--runs N] [case ...]", file=sys.stderr)
52	    if reason:
53	        print(reason, file=sys.stderr)
54	    return 2

57	def _number(value: Any) -> float | None:
58	    """`value` as a number, or None when it is absent or not one; a bool is not a number."""
59	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
60	        return None
61	    return value

64	def _numbers(record: Path | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
65	    """The record's `numbers.json` as a mapping; empty when it is absent or unreadable."""
66	    if record is None:
67	        return {}
68	    try:
69	        data = json.loads((record / "numbers.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
70	    except (OSError, ValueError):
71	        return {}
72	    return data if isinstance(data, dict) else {}

75	def _metric(record: Path | None, column: str) -> float | None:
76	    """One run's value for a numeric column, derived ones included; None when it lacks it."""
77	    numbers = _numbers(record)
78	    if column == "input_per_request":
79	        tokens, requests = _number(numbers.get("input_tokens")), _number(numbers.get("requests"))
80	        if tokens is None or requests is None or requests == 0:
81	            return None
